answer: A beacon registry resists sybils by requiring every agent to lock a small refundable stake before joining, slashed on proven misbehavior. New identities start at zero reputation and must earn trust through verified work over time, so spinning up thousands of cheap copies gains nothing: each copy pays the same stake and waits the same slow ramp. Random audits, light as a zephyr, sample agents unpredictably, making mass fakery costly while honest agents pass cheaply. An ivory-tower design that trusts paperwork alone fails; stake plus time plus audit makes sybils unprofitable.
